title: TLS certificate
subtitle: The certificate the WebUI serves. Changes take effect within seconds — nothing restarts.
noneHint: Yagra generates a self-signed certificate on its first start. If this persists, check the core logs.

sourceHint.self_signed: Generated by Yagra and renewed automatically. Browsers will warn until you import your own.
sourceHint.imported: Imported by an operator. Yagra will never replace it on its own.
sourceHint.unknown: Written by a newer version of Yagra. Treated as imported, so it will not be replaced automatically.

current.heading: Currently serving
current.subject: Subject
current.fingerprintHint: Compare this with what your browser shows to confirm you are talking to this server.
current.downloadHint: Add it to a trust store, or point Prometheus and curl at it, while running on a self-signed certificate.

expiry.renewNote: A self-signed certificate renews itself automatically before it expires.

warning.notMaterialized: Stored, but the web server has not picked it up yet. This normally clears within seconds; if it does not, the core logs say why.
warning.keyUnreadable: The private key can no longer be decrypted — the encryption key has changed or been lost. The certificate cannot be renewed or re-served until you import it again. Restore the KEK file if you still have it.
warning.apiPortPublic: Yagra's API port is still reachable over plain HTTP from the network. Browsers do not use it, but Prometheus, webhook senders and scripts might. Once they are all using this HTTPS address with a certificate they trust, set YAGRA_API_BIND=127.0.0.1 to close it.
warning.apiPortPublicTitle: The encrypted address is not the only way in

import.heading: Import a certificate
import.intro: Paste or upload the certificate chain and its private key, in PEM. Yagra checks that they belong together before installing anything.
import.certificateHint: Leaf certificate first, followed by any intermediates.
import.privateKeyHint: Not passphrase-protected. This is stored encrypted and is never shown again.
import.success: Certificate imported. It is live now.

block.certificate-not-pem: That does not look like a PEM certificate — it should begin with -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----.
block.certificate-has-key: That is a private key, not a certificate. Put it in the private-key field: the certificate is stored unencrypted and can be downloaded, so a key here would be exposed.
block.key-missing: Paste or upload the private key.
block.key-not-pem: That does not look like a PEM private key.
block.key-encrypted: This key is passphrase-protected and cannot be read. Convert it first: openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt -in key.pem -out key-plain.pem

regenerate.heading: Regenerate the self-signed certificate
regenerate.intro: Useful when the browser warns about the name rather than the issuer. Yagra cannot know the address you browse to, so the generated certificate covers only loopback and the server's own hostname unless you list more here.
regenerate.namesHint: One per line or comma-separated. Leave empty for the defaults.
regenerate.success: New self-signed certificate generated and applied.
regenerate.confirm: Replace the certificate currently being served?
regenerate.confirmImported: This will replace the certificate you imported with a new self-signed one. Browsers will start warning again. Continue?
